product_summary.goal: Deliver an original offline-first Windows 2D arcade game in Godot where players convert momentum into destruction and destruction rewards back into momentum through skillful routing, progression, and repeat competitive runs.
users: Players who enjoy route optimization, progression, and repeated mastery attempts
Casual players who need immediately understandable controls without removing the high skill ceiling
non_goals: Photo mode or automatic highlight capture
Daily challenges, seasons, live events, or live-operations systems
Official mod support or Workshop integration
Cloud saves, multiple profiles, full accounts, social features, or cross-device progression
Dynamic weather, day/night variants, story, cutscenes, cinematic menus, or animated garage presentation
Advanced structural destruction simulation or collidable debris fields

safety_boundaries: Use original code, names, art, audio, branding, and level layouts; do not copy proprietary material from the inspiration.
Keep destruction family-friendly and non-graphic, with no injured people, blood, suffering, or realistic consequences.
Record source, author, license, permitted use, and attribution requirements for every external asset before inclusion.
Paid or supporter content must remain cosmetic-only and must never alter physics, scoring, progression power, resources, unlocks, or leaderboard eligibility.
Crash reporting is opt-in and excludes saves, screenshots, recordings, personal information, continuous telemetry, and background uploads.
Public release builds expose no developer cheats, debug controls, or diagnostic overlays.
No contributor may silently move accepted post-MVP scope into the MVP.

repo_split.name: destructro-truck
repo_split.purpose: Single product repository containing the Godot client, deterministic gameplay domain, backend services, tools, tests, assets, and Assembly Line planning artifacts.
contains: src/core for shared contracts, deterministic domain types, configuration, and event definitions
src/gameplay for truck physics, launch, momentum, collision, camera, and run viability
src/world for buildings, wrecks, aerial objects, pickups, deterministic schedules, and level runtime
src/run for game modes, scoring, progression, upgrades, equipment, radar, achievements, statistics, and save orchestration
src/ui for input abstraction, menus, HUD, settings, hints, localization, and presentation adapters
backend for leaderboard, validation, anonymous identity/progression reconciliation, and crash-report services
assets for original and licensed presentation content with attribution records
tests for deterministic domain, save, run-record, integration, and performance verification
tools for level candidate generation, validation, build/export, and developer utilities

frontend_screens.name: Main Menu
frontend_screens.notes: Fast functional entry to Play, Upgrades, Customization, Statistics, Settings, and Help. No animated garage or cinematic background.

frontend_screens.name: Mode and Level Select
frontend_screens.notes: Clearly explains temporary boosts being disabled in Stock attempts.

frontend_screens.name: Pre-Run Loadout
frontend_screens.notes: Compact and skippable for Instant Restart where rules permit.

frontend_screens.name: Gameplay HUD
frontend_screens.notes: Must remain readable at high speed and at mobile-scale layouts.

frontend_screens.name: Run Results
frontend_screens.notes: Supports normal result review and minimal-delay Instant Restart.

frontend_screens.name: Upgrades and Equipment
frontend_screens.notes: No branching-tree visualization is required; mostly independent upgrade cards are sufficient.

frontend_screens.name: Customization
frontend_screens.notes: Strictly cosmetic; default plus one alternate per accepted category.

frontend_screens.name: Statistics
frontend_screens.notes: No graphs, histories, exports, or extra tracking.

frontend_screens.name: Leaderboards
renders_from: ranked entries by level, mode, and category
frontend_screens.notes: Shows only rank, display name, score, date, truck, level, and category.

frontend_screens.name: Settings and Help
renders_from: audio, display, quality, controls, accessibility, language-ready text, Instant Restart, and reviewed hints
frontend_screens.notes: Essential controls only; advanced diagnostics remain development-only.

backend_services.name: Leaderboard Query and Submission Service
backend_services.responsibility: Receive compact run records, route them through validation, persist accepted leaderboard entries, return ranked pages, and enforce duplicate/version/expiry rules.
outputs: accepted/rejected submission result with reason code

backend_services.name: Run Plausibility Validation Service
backend_services.responsibility: Validate schemas, signatures, event ordering, score arithmetic, resource limits, movement envelopes, ruleset compatibility, duplicates, replay attempts, clock anomalies, and obvious impossibilities without deterministic physics replay.

backend_services.name: Anonymous Identity and Progression Reconciliation Service
backend_services.responsibility: Issue and rotate device-bound profile credentials, reconcile signed ordered progression transactions, reject duplicate or impossible ledgers, and support one-time recovery-code transfer with one active identity.

backend_services.name: Crash Report Intake Service
backend_services.responsibility: Accept explicitly consented crash reports containing only approved diagnostics and retain enough metadata for triage.

core_engine_responsibilities: Provide a Godot project skeleton with deterministic configuration loading and development/release feature flags.
Separate Godot physics nodes from deterministic domain calculations and versioned gameplay data.
Own truck launch, body/wheel behavior, camera following, capped aerial rotation, nudge impulses, momentum accounting, contact classification, and run viability detection.
Publish normalized GameplayEvents rather than letting scoring, progression, or UI inspect physics nodes directly.
Instantiate versioned fixed-layout levels and deterministic world-object schedules.
Apply building intact-to-wreck transitions, fixed speed costs, visual-only debris, and data-driven impulse rewards.
Orchestrate Survival and Timed Efficiency through ruleset strategies sharing the same gameplay runtime.
Calculate score, rewards, progression transactions, achievements, statistics, and leaderboard eligibility from versioned domain rules.
Persist one local profile through atomic temporary-write replacement and one automatic backup.
Produce compact run records and maintain an offline submission queue without requiring connectivity for gameplay.
Expose read-only presentation models to UI and keep input routed through action abstractions compatible with later touch controls.
Support debug hitboxes, event tracing, deterministic fixtures, and placeholder-first gameplay validation without exposing tools in release builds.
verification_tasks: Validate all planning JSON against the AI Assembly Line contracts before planning PR review.
Create headless tests for deterministic score breakdowns, mode rules, upgrade effects, progression transactions, achievement evaluation, and leaderboard eligibility.
Create save tests covering atomic replacement, backup restoration, schema/version rejection, and corrupted primary saves.
Create compact run-record fixtures covering valid submissions, malformed records, duplicate/replayed records, impossible score/resource changes, clock anomalies, and ruleset mismatches.
Create grey-box manual playtest scenarios for launch, building destruction, fixed speed loss, wreck bounce, balloon recovery, aerial routing, run termination, and instant restart.
Create deterministic schedule tests for moving plane/satellite-like objects and fixed level layouts.
Create input tests for keyboard/gamepad action parity and press-versus-hold nudge behavior.
Create UI accessibility checks for scalable text, non-color-only information, reduced shake/flash, and meaningful audio equivalents.
Create performance scenes with maximum expected buildings, visual debris, particles, and aerial objects; verify cosmetic scaling does not change gameplay results.
Create Windows export/build verification and confirm development-only tools are absent from release builds.
Require recorded gameplay evidence and a manual MVP acceptance checklist before release acceptance.
Use red-team review for shared contracts, scoring/physics changes, saves, run records, identity/recovery, backend validation, cross-lane changes, and release candidates.

starter_prompts.intake_interviewer: Read merged intake and requirements only. Preserve the accepted MVP boundary and route new ideas to explicit change control or post-MVP notes.
starter_prompts.planning_agent: Define architecture, contracts, file ownership, verification, and topologically compatible implementation lanes without creating executable tasks or changing accepted requirements.
starter_prompts.contract_steward: Own shared event, data, save, ruleset, API, and validation contracts. Land contract definitions before dependent lane implementation and reject undocumented coupling.
starter_prompts.frontend_builder: Own input abstraction, presentation models, menus, HUD, settings, hints, localization hooks, and VFX/audio adapters. Consume domain contracts; do not inspect physics internals or invent gameplay state.
starter_prompts.backend_builder: Own leaderboard, plausibility validation, anonymous identity/progression reconciliation, crash intake, service schemas, and deployment boundaries. Do not require connectivity for local gameplay.
starter_prompts.core_engine_builder: Own deterministic gameplay/domain implementation across truck physics boundaries, world runtime, run orchestration, scoring, progression, saves, and compact run-record production according to assigned file ownership.
starter_prompts.red_team_verifier: Adversarially inspect any selected task or integration boundary for scope drift, exploits, nondeterminism, false-positive tests, save/progression abuse, leaderboard cheating, privacy violations, and missing evidence. Report concrete findings without changing requirements or merging work.
